concepts.display: Prescription Item is not fully dispensed (this value has also to be set to resume a prescription after “on-hold”)

extra.case_scenario_examples:
Scenario 1: Prescription is newly issued and ready for first dispense.
Scenario 2: The prescription was previously on-hold (e.g., pending clarification or stock availability) and has now been resumed — it becomes active again so dispensing can continue.
Scenario 3: The pharmacist dispensed part of the prescribed quantity (partial dispense) and the remaining quantity is still pending.

Scenario 1: The prescriber has paused the prescription pending physician approval, clinical clarification, or patient review.
Scenario 2: The item is placed on-hold due to stock unavailability and will resume once the issue is resolved.

Scenario 1: The pharmacist dispensed the entire prescribed quantity, and no remaining quantities exist.
Scenario 2: A multi-dispense prescription reached its final dispense event, so no further dispensing is permitted.

concepts.display: The prescription has been voided or withdrawn. Cancellation can occur before or after dispensing — however, if performed after dispensing, it is considered a discontinuation.

extra.case_scenario_examples:
Scenario 1: The prescriber voided the prescription due to an entry error before any dispense occurred.
Scenario 2: The prescriber discontinues the prescription after a dispense due to a clinical reason — for example, an adverse reaction or patient allergy discovered post-dispensation.
Example 3: A duplicate or test prescription was identified and withdrawn

concepts.display: Prescription Item is stopped, before full dispensation(s) already occurred, and can also be interpreted as an expiry.

extra.case_scenario_examples:
Scenario 1: The prescriber instructed to stop the therapy mid-course due to change in treatment plan.
Scenario 2: The controlled prescription automatically stops (expires) when the end date provided in the MedicationRequest is reached. In this case, the Raqeeb system automatically updates the status to stopped and no further dispensing is permitted.

definition: Indicates the current state of a prescription item within the medication management workflow.
